title: Member Handbook — Your Personal Care Hours in Care Management, Reductions and Choosing Your Attendant
content:
If your Care Management tier authorizes personal care hours, two protections apply to them: how a reduction of your authorized hours takes effect, and your right, where your tier allows it, to direct your own attendant.

## A reduction of your hours

A reduction of authorized hours takes effect only after the tier's advance notice period, counted in calendar days, of written notice with appeal rights. Until that written notice, with your appeal rights, has run for the full number of days, your authorized hours are not reduced.

| Written notice given | Notice includes appeal rights | Notice period has run | Notice condition for the reduction met |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Yes | No | Yes | No |
| No | — | — | No |

*Hypothetical example:* in a tier with a 10-day notice period, written notice with appeal rights is dated 1 September. On 5 September only 4 calendar days of that notice have passed, so the reduction has not taken effect.

## Directing your own attendant

Where your tier allows it, you may direct your own attendant, including a relative who is not legally responsible for you. Whether each of these is allowed is set tier by tier: your tier may allow you to direct your own attendant, and may separately allow a relative who is not legally responsible for you to be paid as your attendant.

## Questions answered

**Can my nephew be my paid attendant?** Where your tier allows a relative who is not legally responsible for you to be paid as attendant, a nephew who is not legally responsible for you may be.

**Does the reduction start on the day I receive the letter?** No. It takes effect only after the notice period has run on written notice that includes your appeal rights.
